question: Lack of sufficient competition in public procurement in Greece with single bidders in 55 % of procedures

According to the Commission's official Single Market and Competitiveness Scoreboard, in 2024 in Greece, 55 % of public procurement procedures in which the relevant indicator is measured ended with a single bidder, compared to an EU average of 28 %. The extremely high percentage of procedures with only one bidder raises reasonable questions as to the degree of real competition, access of businesses to public procurement and the efficient use of public and European funds. In light of the above: 1.
How does the Commission assess the fact that the percentage of procedures with a single bidder in Greece is 55 %, almost double the EU average?
Has the Commission identified structural problems in the design or operation of Greek public procurement procedures that restrict competition, in particular in contracts cofinanced by EU funds?
What supervisory measures, recommendations or other actions does the Commission intend to take to increase competition and ensure the effective and transparent use of European funds in Greece?
